label: agnosia
semantic_ground_truth: Loss of the ability to comprehend the meaning or recognize the importance of various forms of stimulation that cannot be attributed to impairment of a primary sensory modality. Tactile agnosia is characterized by an inability to perceive the shape and nature of an object by touch alone, despite unimpaired sensation to light touch, position, and other primary sensory modalities.

label: agraphia
semantic_ground_truth: Loss or impairment of the ability to write (letters, syllables, words, or phrases) due to an injury to a specific cerebral area or occasionally due to emotional factors. This condition rarely occurs in isolation, and often accompanies APHASIA. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p485; APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994)

label: alcohol amnestic disorder
semantic_ground_truth: A mental disorder associated with chronic ethanol abuse (ALCOHOLISM) and nutritional deficiencies characterized by short term memory loss, confabulations, and disturbances of attention. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1139)

label: alcohol withdrawal delirium
semantic_ground_truth: An acute organic mental disorder induced by cessation or reduction in chronic alcohol consumption. Clinical characteristics include CONFUSION; DELUSIONS; vivid HALLUCINATIONS; TREMOR; agitation; insomnia; and signs of autonomic hyperactivity (e.g., elevated blood pressure and heart rate, dilated pupils, and diaphoresis). This condition may occasionally be fatal. It was formerly called delirium tremens. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1175)

label: alcoholic intoxication
semantic_ground_truth: An acute brain syndrome which results from the excessive ingestion of ETHANOL or ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES.

label: alcoholism
semantic_ground_truth: A primary, chronic disease with genetic, psychosocial, and environmental factors influencing its development and manifestations. The disease is often progressive and fatal. It is characterized by impaired control over drinking, preoccupation with the drug alcohol, use of alcohol despite adverse consequences, and distortions in thinking, most notably denial. Each of these symptoms may be continuous or periodic. (Morse & Flavin for the Joint Commission of the National Council on Alcoholism and Drug Dependence and the American Society of Addiction Medicine to Study the Definition and Criteria for the Diagnosis of Alcoholism: in JAMA 1992;268:1012-4)

label: alzheimer disease
semantic_ground_truth: A degenerative disease of the BRAIN characterized by the insidious onset of DEMENTIA. Impairment of MEMORY, judgment, attention span, and problem solving skills are followed by severe APRAXIAS and a global loss of cognitive abilities. The condition primarily occurs after age 60, and is marked pathologically by severe cortical atrophy and the triad of SENILE PLAQUES; NEUROFIBRILLARY TANGLES; and NEUROPIL THREADS. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1049-57)

label: amnesia
semantic_ground_truth: Pathologic partial or complete loss of the ability to recall past experiences (AMNESIA, RETROGRADE) or to form new memories (AMNESIA, ANTEROGRADE). This condition may be of organic or psychologic origin. Organic forms of amnesia are usually associated with dysfunction of the DIENCEPHALON or HIPPOCAMPUS. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp426-7)

label: amnesia, retrograde
semantic_ground_truth: Loss of the ability to recall information that had been previously encoded in memory prior to a specified or approximate point in time. This process may be organic or psychogenic in origin. Organic forms may be associated with CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA; CEREBROVASCULAR ACCIDENTS; SEIZURES; DEMENTIA; and a wide variety of other conditions that impair cerebral function. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp426-9)

label: feeding and eating disorders
semantic_ground_truth: A group of disorders characterized by physiological and/or psychological disturbances in appetite or food intake.

label: apraxias
semantic_ground_truth: A group of cognitive disorders characterized by the inability to perform previously learned skills that cannot be attributed to deficits of motor or sensory function. The two major subtypes of this condition are ideomotor (see APRAXIA, IDEOMOTOR) and ideational apraxia, which refers to loss of the ability to mentally formulate the processes involved with performing an action. For example, dressing apraxia may result from an inability to mentally formulate the act of placing clothes on the body. Apraxias are generally associated with lesions of the dominant PARIETAL LOBE and supramarginal gyrus. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp56-7)

label: auditory perceptual disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Acquired or developmental cognitive disorders of AUDITORY PERCEPTION characterized by a reduced ability to perceive information contained in auditory stimuli despite intact auditory pathways. Affected individuals have difficulty with speech perception, sound localization, and comprehending the meaning of inflections of speech.

label: back pain
semantic_ground_truth: Acute or chronic pain located in the posterior regions of the THORAX; LUMBOSACRAL REGION; or the adjacent regions.

label: bruxism
semantic_ground_truth: A disorder characterized by grinding and clenching of the teeth.

label: burnout, professional
semantic_ground_truth: An excessive stress reaction to one's occupational or professional environment. It may be characterized by feelings of emotional and physical exhaustion, coupled with a sense of frustration and failure.

label: marijuana abuse
semantic_ground_truth: Use of marijuana associated with abnormal psychological, social, and or occupational functioning.

label: cataplexy
semantic_ground_truth: A condition characterized by transient weakness or paralysis of somatic musculature triggered by an emotional stimulus or physical exertion. Cataplexy is frequently associated with NARCOLEPSY. During a cataplectic attack, there is a marked reduction in muscle tone similar to the normal physiologic hypotonia that accompanies rapid eye movement sleep (SLEEP, REM). (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p396)

label: catatonia
semantic_ground_truth: A neuropsychiatric disorder characterized by one or more of the following essential features: immobility, mutism, negativism (active or passive refusal to follow commands), mannerisms, stereotypies, posturing, grimacing, excitement, echolalia, echopraxia, muscular rigidity, and stupor; sometimes punctuated by sudden violent outbursts, panic, or hallucinations. This condition may be associated with psychiatric illnesses (e.g., SCHIZOPHRENIA; MOOD DISORDERS) or organic disorders (NEUROLEPTIC MALIGNANT SYNDROME; ENCEPHALITIS, etc.). (From DSM-IV, 4th ed, 1994; APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994)

label: chest pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pressure, burning, or numbness in the chest.

label: communication disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Disorders of verbal and nonverbal communication caused by receptive or expressive LANGUAGE DISORDERS, cognitive dysfunction (e.g., MENTAL RETARDATION), psychiatric conditions, and HEARING DISORDERS.

label: confusion
semantic_ground_truth: A mental state characterized by bewilderment, emotional disturbance, lack of clear thinking, and perceptual disorientation.

label: consciousness disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Organic mental disorders in which there is impairment of the ability to maintain awareness of self and environment and to respond to environmental stimuli. Dysfunction of the cerebral hemispheres or brain stem RETICULAR FORMATION may result in this condition.

label: delirium
semantic_ground_truth: A disorder characterized by CONFUSION; inattentiveness; disorientation; ILLUSIONS; HALLUCINATIONS; agitation; and in some instances autonomic nervous system overactivity. It may result from toxic/metabolic conditions or structural brain lesions. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp411-2)

label: dementia
semantic_ground_truth: An acquired organic mental disorder with loss of intellectual abilities of sufficient severity to interfere with social or occupational functioning. The dysfunction is multifaceted and involves memory, behavior, personality, judgment, attention, spatial relations, language, abstract thought, and other executive functions. The intellectual decline is usually progressive, and initially spares the level of consciousness.

label: dyslexia
semantic_ground_truth: A cognitive disorder characterized by an impaired ability to comprehend written and printed words or phrases despite intact vision. This condition may be developmental or acquired. Developmental dyslexia is marked by reading achievement that falls substantially below that expected given the individual's chronological age, measured intelligence, and age-appropriate education. The disturbance in reading significantly interferes with academic achievement or with activities of daily living that require reading skills. (From DSM-IV)

label: dyslexia, acquired
semantic_ground_truth: A receptive visual aphasia characterized by the loss of a previously possessed ability to comprehend the meaning or significance of handwritten words, despite intact vision. This condition may be associated with posterior cerebral artery infarction (INFARCTION, POSTERIOR CEREBRAL ARTERY) and other BRAIN DISEASES.

label: dyspareunia
semantic_ground_truth: Recurrent genital pain occurring during, before, or after SEXUAL INTERCOURSE in either the male or the female.

label: earache
semantic_ground_truth: Pain in the ear.

label: encopresis
semantic_ground_truth: Incontinence of feces not due to organic defect or illness.

label: enuresis
semantic_ground_truth: Involuntary discharge of URINE after expected age of completed development of urinary control. This can happen during the daytime (DIURNAL ENURESIS) while one is awake or during sleep (NOCTURNAL ENURESIS). Enuresis can be in children or in adults (as persistent primary enuresis and secondary adult-onset enuresis).

label: facial pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pain in the facial region including orofacial pain and craniofacial pain. Associated conditions include local inflammatory and neoplastic disorders and neuralgic syndromes involving the trigeminal, facial, and glossopharyngeal nerves. Conditions which feature recurrent or persistent facial pain as the primary manifestation of disease are referred to as FACIAL PAIN SYNDROMES.

label: mental fatigue
semantic_ground_truth: A condition of low alertness or cognitive impairment, usually associated with prolonged mental activities or stress.

label: gagging
semantic_ground_truth: Contraction of the muscle of the PHARYNX caused by stimulation of sensory receptors on the SOFT PALATE, by psychic stimuli, or systemically by drugs.

label: gerstmann syndrome
semantic_ground_truth: A disorder of cognition characterized by the tetrad of finger agnosia, dysgraphia, DYSCALCULIA, and right-left disorientation. The syndrome may be developmental or acquired. Acquired Gerstmann syndrome is associated with lesions in the dominant (usually left) PARIETAL LOBE which involve the angular gyrus or subjacent white matter. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p457)

label: tourette syndrome
semantic_ground_truth: A neuropsychological disorder related to alterations in DOPAMINE metabolism and neurotransmission involving frontal-subcortical neuronal circuits. Both multiple motor and one or more vocal tics need to be present with TICS occurring many times a day, nearly daily, over a period of more than one year. The onset is before age 18 and the disturbance is not due to direct physiological effects of a substance or another medical condition. The disturbance causes marked distress or significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning. (From DSM-IV, 1994; Neurol Clin 1997 May;15(2):357-79)

label: huntington disease
semantic_ground_truth: A familial disorder inherited as an autosomal dominant trait and characterized by the onset of progressive CHOREA and DEMENTIA in the fourth or fifth decade of life. Common initial manifestations include paranoia; poor impulse control; DEPRESSION; HALLUCINATIONS; and DELUSIONS. Eventually intellectual impairment; loss of fine motor control; ATHETOSIS; and diffuse chorea involving axial and limb musculature develops, leading to a vegetative state within 10-15 years of disease onset. The juvenile variant has a more fulminant course including SEIZURES; ATAXIA; dementia; and chorea. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1060-4)

label: creutzfeldt-jakob syndrome
semantic_ground_truth: A rare transmissible encephalopathy most prevalent between the ages of 50 and 70 years. Affected individuals may present with sleep disturbances, personality changes, ATAXIA; APHASIA, visual loss, weakness, muscle atrophy, MYOCLONUS, progressive dementia, and death within one year of disease onset. A familial form exhibiting autosomal dominant inheritance and a new variant CJD (potentially associated with ENCEPHALOPATHY, BOVINE SPONGIFORM) have been described. Pathological features include prominent cerebellar and cerebral cortical spongiform degeneration and the presence of PRIONS. (From N Engl J Med, 1998 Dec 31;339(27))

label: intellectual disability
semantic_ground_truth: Subnormal intellectual functioning which originates during the developmental period. This has multiple potential etiologies, including genetic defects and perinatal insults. Intelligence quotient (IQ) scores are commonly used to determine whether an individual has an intellectual disability. IQ scores between 70 and 79 are in the borderline range. Scores below 67 are in the disabled range. (from Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1992, Ch55, p28)

label: morphine dependence
semantic_ground_truth: Strong dependence, both physiological and emotional, upon morphine.

label: mutism
semantic_ground_truth: The inability to generate oral-verbal expression, despite normal comprehension of speech. This may be associated with BRAIN DISEASES or MENTAL DISORDERS. Organic mutism may be associated with damage to the FRONTAL LOBE; BRAIN STEM; THALAMUS; and CEREBELLUM. Selective mutism is a psychological condition that usually affects children characterized by continuous refusal to speak in social situations by a child who is able and willing to speak to selected persons. Kussmal aphasia refers to mutism in psychosis. (From Fortschr Neurol Psychiatr 1994; 62(9):337-44)

label: narcolepsy
semantic_ground_truth: A condition characterized by recurrent episodes of daytime somnolence and lapses in consciousness (microsomnias) that may be associated with automatic behaviors and AMNESIA. CATAPLEXY; SLEEP PARALYSIS, and hypnagogic HALLUCINATIONS frequently accompany narcolepsy. The pathophysiology of this disorder includes sleep-onset rapid eye movement (REM) sleep, which normally follows stage III or IV sleep. (From Neurology 1998 Feb;50(2 Suppl 1):S2-S7)

label: opioid-related disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Disorders related to or resulting from abuse or misuse of OPIOIDS.

label: neonatal abstinence syndrome
semantic_ground_truth: Fetal and neonatal addiction and withdrawal as a result of the mother's dependence on drugs during pregnancy. Withdrawal or abstinence symptoms develop shortly after birth. Symptoms exhibited are loud, high-pitched crying, sweating, yawning and gastrointestinal disturbances.

label: neuralgia
semantic_ground_truth: Intense or aching pain that occurs along the course or distribution of a peripheral or cranial nerve.

label: pain

label: intractable pain

label: postoperative pain

label: perceptual disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Cognitive disorders characterized by an impaired ability to perceive the nature of objects or concepts through use of the sense organs. These include spatial neglect syndromes, where an individual does not attend to visual, auditory, or sensory stimuli presented from one side of the body.

label: phantom limb
semantic_ground_truth: Perception of painful and nonpainful phantom sensations that occur following the complete or partial loss of a limb. The majority of individuals with an amputated extremity will experience the impression that the limb is still present, and in many cases, painful. (From Neurol Clin 1998 Nov;16(4):919-36; Brain 1998 Sep;121(Pt 9):1603-30)

label: phencyclidine abuse
semantic_ground_truth: The misuse of phencyclidine with associated psychological symptoms and impairment in social or occupational functioning.

label: pica
semantic_ground_truth: The persistent eating of non-nutritive substances for a period of at least one month.

label: psychomotor agitation
semantic_ground_truth: A feeling of restlessness associated with increased motor activity. This may occur as a manifestation of nervous system drug toxicity or other conditions.

label: psychomotor disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Abnormalities of motor function that are associated with organic and non-organic cognitive disorders.

label: psychoses, alcoholic
semantic_ground_truth: A group of mental disorders associated with organic brain damage and caused by poisoning from alcohol.

label: psychoses, substance-induced
semantic_ground_truth: Psychotic organic mental disorders resulting from the toxic effect of drugs and chemicals or other harmful substance.

label: restless legs syndrome
semantic_ground_truth: A disorder characterized by aching or burning sensations in the lower and rarely the upper extremities that occur prior to sleep or may awaken the patient from sleep.

label: self mutilation
semantic_ground_truth: The act of injuring one's own body to the extent of cutting off or permanently destroying a limb or other essential part of a body.

label: sleep deprivation
semantic_ground_truth: The state of being deprived of sleep under experimental conditions, due to life events, or from a wide variety of pathophysiologic causes such as medication effect, chronic illness, psychiatric illness, or sleep disorder.

label: sleep wake disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Abnormal sleep-wake schedule or pattern associated with the CIRCADIAN RHYTHM which affect the length, timing, and/or rigidity of the sleep-wake cycle relative to the day-night cycle.

label: somnambulism
semantic_ground_truth: A parasomnia characterized by a partial arousal that occurs during stage IV of non-REM sleep. Affected individuals exhibit semipurposeful behaviors such as ambulation and are difficult to fully awaken. Children are primarily affected, with a peak age range of 4-6 years.

label: substance withdrawal syndrome
semantic_ground_truth: Physiological and psychological symptoms associated with withdrawal from the use of a drug after prolonged administration or habituation. The concept includes withdrawal from smoking or drinking, as well as withdrawal from an administered drug.

label: tic disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Disorders characterized by recurrent TICS that may interfere with speech and other activities. Tics are sudden, rapid, nonrhythmic, stereotyped motor movements or vocalizations which may be exacerbated by stress and are generally attenuated during absorbing activities. Tic disorders are distinguished from conditions which feature other types of abnormal movements that may accompany another another condition. (From DSM-IV, 1994)

label: wernicke encephalopathy

label: crowding

label: crying

label: dance therapy

label: dangerous behavior

label: defense mechanisms
semantic_ground_truth: Unconscious process used by an individual or a group of individuals in order to cope with impulses, feelings or ideas which are not acceptable at their conscious level; various types include reaction formation, projection and self reversal.

label: delirium
semantic_ground_truth: A disorder characterized by CONFUSION; inattentiveness; disorientation; ILLUSIONS; HALLUCINATIONS; agitation; and in some instances autonomic nervous system overactivity. label: delusions
semantic_ground_truth: A false belief regarding the self or persons or objects outside the self that persists despite the facts, and is not considered tenable by one's associates.

label: dementia
semantic_ground_truth: An acquired organic mental disorder with loss of intellectual abilities of sufficient severity to interfere with social or occupational functioning. The dysfunction is multifaceted and involves memory, behavior, personality, judgment, attention, spatial relations, language, abstract thought, and other executive functions. label: denial, psychological

label: dentist-patient relations

label: dependency, psychological

label: depersonalization

(APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

label: depression

label: desensitization, psychologic

label: behavioral disciplines and activities

label: displacement, psychological

label: dyslexia
semantic_ground_truth: A cognitive disorder characterized by an impaired ability to comprehend written and printed words or phrases despite intact vision. label: dyslexia, acquired

label: psychiatry
semantic_ground_truth: The medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders.

label: psychoacoustics
semantic_ground_truth: The science pertaining to the interrelationship of psychologic phenomena and the individual's response to the physical properties of sound.

label: psychoanalysis
semantic_ground_truth: The separation or resolution of the psyche into its constituent elements. The term has two separate meanings: 1. a procedure devised by Sigmund Freud, for investigating mental processes by means of free association, dream interpretation and interpretation of resistance and transference manifestations; and 2. a theory of psychology developed by Freud from his clinical experience with hysterical patients. (From Campbell, Psychiatric Dictionary, 1996).

label: psychoanalytic interpretation
semantic_ground_truth: Utilization of Freudian theories to explain various psychologic aspects of art, literature, biographical material, etc.

label: psychoanalytic therapy
semantic_ground_truth: A form of psychiatric treatment, based on Freudian principles, which seeks to eliminate or diminish the undesirable effects of unconscious conflicts by making the patient aware of their existence, origin, and inappropriate expression in current emotions and behavior.

label: psychodrama
semantic_ground_truth: Primarily a technique of group psychotherapy which involves a structured, directed, and dramatized acting out of the patient's personal and emotional problems.

label: psycholinguistics
semantic_ground_truth: A discipline concerned with relations between messages and the characteristics of individuals who select and interpret them; it deals directly with the processes of encoding (phonetics) and decoding (psychoacoustics) as they relate states of messages to states of communicators.

label: psychological techniques
semantic_ground_truth: Methods used in the diagnosis and treatment of behavioral, personality, and mental disorders.

label: psychological tests
semantic_ground_truth: Standardized tests designed to measure abilities (as in intelligence, aptitude, and achievement tests) or to evaluate personality traits.

label: psychology
semantic_ground_truth: The science dealing with the study of mental processes and behavior in man and animals.

label: psychology, clinical
semantic_ground_truth: The branch of psychology concerned with psychological methods of recognizing and treating behavior disorders.

label: psychology, comparative
semantic_ground_truth: The branch of psychology concerned with similarities or differences in the behavior of different animal species or of different races or peoples.

label: psychology, educational
semantic_ground_truth: The branch of psychology concerned with psychological aspects of teaching and the formal learning process in school.

label: psychology, experimental
semantic_ground_truth: The branch of psychology which seeks to learn more about the fundamental causes of behavior by studying various psychologic phenomena in controlled experimental situations.

label: psychology, industrial
semantic_ground_truth: The branch of applied psychology concerned with the application of psychologic principles and methods to industrial problems including selection and training of workers, working conditions, etc.

label: psychology, medical
semantic_ground_truth: A branch of psychology in which there is collaboration between psychologists and physicians in the management of medical problems. It differs from clinical psychology, which is concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of behavior disorders.

label: psychology, social
semantic_ground_truth: The branch of psychology concerned with the effects of group membership upon the behavior, attitudes, and beliefs of an individual.

label: psychometrics
semantic_ground_truth: Assessment of psychological variables by the application of mathematical procedures.

label: psychomotor agitation
semantic_ground_truth: A feeling of restlessness associated with increased motor activity. This may occur as a manifestation of nervous system drug toxicity or other conditions.

label: psychomotor disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Abnormalities of motor function that are associated with organic and non-organic cognitive disorders.

label: psychomotor performance
semantic_ground_truth: The coordination of a sensory or ideational (cognitive) process and a motor activity.

label: psychoneuroimmunology
semantic_ground_truth: The field concerned with the interrelationship between the brain, behavior and the immune system. Neuropsychologic, neuroanatomic and psychosocial studies have demonstrated their role in accentuating or diminishing immune/allergic responses.

label: psychopathology
semantic_ground_truth: The study of significant causes and processes in the development of mental illness.

label: psychopharmacology
semantic_ground_truth: The study of the effects of drugs on mental and behavioral activity.

label: psychophysics
semantic_ground_truth: The science dealing with the correlation of the physical characteristics of a stimulus, e.g., frequency or intensity, with the response to the stimulus, in order to assess the psychologic factors involved in the relationship.

label: psychophysiology
semantic_ground_truth: The study of the physiological basis of human and animal behavior.

historical_trace.history_note: MIND-BODY RELATIONS (PHYSIOLOGY) was MIND-BODY RELATIONS see PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGY 1996

label: psychoses, alcoholic
semantic_ground_truth: A group of mental disorders associated with organic brain damage and caused by poisoning from alcohol.

label: psychoses, substance-induced
semantic_ground_truth: Psychotic organic mental disorders resulting from the toxic effect of drugs and chemicals or other harmful substance.

label: psychosexual development
semantic_ground_truth: The stages of development of the psychological aspects of sexuality from birth to adulthood; i.e., oral, anal, genital, and latent periods.

label: psychosocial deprivation
semantic_ground_truth: The absence of appropriate stimuli in the physical or social environment which are necessary for the emotional, social, and intellectual development of the individual.

label: psychosomatic medicine
semantic_ground_truth: A system of medicine which aims at discovering the exact nature of the relationship between the emotions and bodily function, affirming the principle that the mind and body are one.

label: psychosurgery
semantic_ground_truth: Treatment of chronic, severe and intractable psychiatric disorders by surgical removal or interruption of certain areas or pathways in the brain, especially in the prefrontal lobes.

label: psychotherapy
semantic_ground_truth: A generic term for the treatment of mental illness or emotional disturbances primarily by verbal or nonverbal communication.

label: psychotherapy, brief
semantic_ground_truth: Any form of psychotherapy designed to produce therapeutic change within a minimal amount of time, generally not more than 20 sessions.

label: psychotherapy, group
semantic_ground_truth: A form of therapy in which two or more patients participate under the guidance of one or more psychotherapists for the purpose of treating emotional disturbances, social maladjustments, and psychotic states.

label: psychotherapy, multiple
semantic_ground_truth: The use of more than one therapist at one time in individual or group psychotherapy.

label: psychotherapy, rational-emotive
semantic_ground_truth: The replacement of illogical and unrealistic ideas with more realistic and adaptive ones through direct intervention and confrontation by the therapist.

label: q-sort
semantic_ground_truth: A personality assessment technique in which the subject or observer indicates the degree to which a standardized set of descriptive statements actually describes the subject. The term reflects sorting procedures occasionally used with this technique.

label: rage
semantic_ground_truth: Fury; violent, intense anger.

label: rationalization
semantic_ground_truth: A defense mechanism operating unconsciously, in which the individual attempts to justify or make consciously tolerable, by plausible means, feelings, behavior, and motives that would otherwise be intolerable.

label: reaction time
semantic_ground_truth: The time from the onset of a stimulus until a response is observed.

historical_trace.history_note: RESPONSE LATENCY was see under REACTION TIME 1970-76

label: reactive inhibition
semantic_ground_truth: Tendency toward a lessened strength of response due to practice or activity. It is independent of the effect of reward and is a direct function of time interval since the last response and the number of preceding responses.

label: reality testing
semantic_ground_truth: The individual's objective evaluation of the external world and the ability to differentiate adequately between it and the internal world; considered to be a primary ego function.

label: reality therapy
semantic_ground_truth: Method of psychotherapeutic treatment based on assumption of patients' personal responsibility for their own behavior. The therapist actively guides patients to accurate self-perception for fulfillment of needs of self-worth and respect for others. (From APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

label: reflex
semantic_ground_truth: An involuntary movement or exercise of function in a part, excited in response to a stimulus applied to the periphery and transmitted to the brain or spinal cord.

historical_trace.history_note: REFLEX, BABINSKI was BABINSKI REFLEX see under REFLEX, ABNORMAL 1968-89

label: refractory period, psychological
semantic_ground_truth: A delayed response interval occurring when two stimuli are presented in close succession.

label: regression, psychology
semantic_ground_truth: A return to earlier, especially to infantile, patterns of thought or behavior, or stage of functioning, e.g., feelings of helplessness and dependency in a patient with a serious physical illness. (From APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994).

label: rejection, psychology
semantic_ground_truth: Non-acceptance, negative attitudes, hostility or excessive criticism of the individual which may precipitate feelings of rejection.

label: relaxation therapy
semantic_ground_truth: Treatment to improve one's health condition by using techniques that can reduce PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS; PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; or both.

label: repression, psychology
semantic_ground_truth: The active mental process of keeping out and ejecting, banishing from consciousness, ideas or impulses that are unacceptable to it.

label: repression-sensitization
semantic_ground_truth: Defense mechanisms involving approach and avoidance responses to threatening stimuli. The sensitizing process involves intellectualization in approaching or controlling the stimulus whereas repression involves unconscious denial in avoiding the stimulus.

label: residential treatment
semantic_ground_truth: A specialized residential treatment program for behavior disorders including substance abuse. It may include therapeutically planned group living and learning situations including teaching of adaptive skills to help patient functioning in the community. (From Kahn, A. P. and Fawcett, J. Encyclopedia of Mental Health, 1993, p320.)

label: restless legs syndrome
semantic_ground_truth: A disorder characterized by aching or burning sensations in the lower and rarely the upper extremities that occur prior to sleep or may awaken the patient from sleep.

label: risk-taking
semantic_ground_truth: Undertaking a task involving a challenge for achievement or a desirable goal in which there is a lack of certainty or a fear of failure. It may also include the exhibiting of certain behaviors whose outcomes may present a risk to the individual or to those associated with him or her.

label: role
semantic_ground_truth: The expected and characteristic pattern of behavior exhibited by an individual as a member of a particular social group.

historical_trace.history_note: 69; ROLE CONCEPT was see under ROLE 1969-78, was see under PSYCHOLOGY, SOCIAL 1966-68

label: role playing
semantic_ground_truth: The adopting or performing the role of another significant individual in order to gain insight into the behavior of that person.

label: rorschach test
semantic_ground_truth: A projective test used to evaluate a broad range of personality variables including pathology of thought and perception. The subject's responses to inkblot prints are scored along with subjective interpretation by the test administrator.

label: scapegoating
semantic_ground_truth: Process in which the mechanisms of projection or displacement are utilized in focusing feelings of aggression, hostility, frustration, etc., upon another individual or group; the amount of blame being unwarranted.

label: schizophrenic language
semantic_ground_truth: The artificial language of schizophrenic patients - neologisms (words of the patient's own making with new meanings).

label: schizophrenic psychology
semantic_ground_truth: Study of mental processes and behavior of schizophrenics.

label: self-assessment
semantic_ground_truth: Appraisal of one's own personal qualities or traits.

label: self concept
semantic_ground_truth: Persons' view of themselves.

historical_trace.history_note: 69; SELF PERCEPTION was see under SELF CONCEPT 1969-78

label: self disclosure
semantic_ground_truth: A willingness to reveal information about oneself to others.

label: self mutilation
semantic_ground_truth: The act of injuring one's own body to the extent of cutting off or permanently destroying a limb or other essential part of a body.

label: self stimulation
semantic_ground_truth: The act or process of inducing or increasing the level of arousal in oneself. It can be observed in various situations; for example, infants who are understimulated may explore their surroundings or babble to themselves.(https://dictionary.apa.org/self-stimulation accessed 12/30/2020)

label: semantic differential
semantic_ground_truth: Analysis of word concepts by the association of polar adjectives, e.g., good-bad, with the concept, father. The adjectives are usually scaled in 7 steps. The subject's placement of the concept on the adjectival scale indicates the connotative meaning of the concept.

label: sensation
semantic_ground_truth: The process in which specialized SENSORY RECEPTOR CELLS transduce peripheral stimuli (physical or chemical) into NERVE IMPULSES which are then transmitted to the various sensory centers in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

label: sensitivity training groups
semantic_ground_truth: A group of people who meet in an unstructured setting to learn about themselves, interpersonal relationships, and group processes and about larger social systems.

label: shame

label: shyness
semantic_ground_truth: Discomfort and partial inhibition of the usual forms of behavior when in the presence of others.

label: sibling relations
semantic_ground_truth: Interactions and relationships between sisters and/or brothers. The concept also applies to animal studies.

label: sick role
semantic_ground_truth: Set of expectations that exempt persons from responsibility for their illness and exempt them from usual responsibilities.

label: sign language
semantic_ground_truth: A system of hand gestures used for communication by those with HEARING LOSS or by people speaking different languages.

historical_trace.history_note: 91(75)63-65; was see under MANUAL COMMUNICATION 1974-90; was heading 1963-65

label: single person
semantic_ground_truth: The unmarried man or woman.

label: sleep
semantic_ground_truth: A readily reversible suspension of sensorimotor interaction with the environment, usually associated with recumbency and immobility.

label: sleep deprivation
semantic_ground_truth: The state of being deprived of sleep under experimental conditions, due to life events, or from a wide variety of pathophysiologic causes such as medication effect, chronic illness, psychiatric illness, or sleep disorder.

label: sleep wake disorders
semantic_ground_truth: Abnormal sleep-wake schedule or pattern associated with the CIRCADIAN RHYTHM which affect the length, timing, and/or rigidity of the sleep-wake cycle relative to the day-night cycle.

label: sleep stages
semantic_ground_truth: Periods of sleep manifested by changes in EEG activity and certain behavioral correlates; they formerly included Stage 1: sleep onset, drowsy sleep; Stage 2: light sleep; Stages 3 and 4: delta sleep, light sleep, deep sleep, telencephalic sleep. In 2007, sleep stages were redefined by The American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) as: N1-N2 (sleep onset - light sleep), N3 (SLOW-WAVE SLEEP), and REM SLEEP.

label: sleep, rem
semantic_ground_truth: A stage of sleep characterized by rapid movements of the eye and low voltage fast pattern EEG. It is usually associated with dreaming.

label: smell
semantic_ground_truth: The ability to detect scents or odors, such as the function of OLFACTORY RECEPTOR NEURONS.

label: smiling
semantic_ground_truth: A facial expression which may denote feelings of pleasure, affection, amusement, etc.

label: smoking
semantic_ground_truth: Willful or deliberate act of inhaling and exhaling SMOKE from burning substances or agents held by hand.

label: social adjustment
semantic_ground_truth: Adaptation of the person to the social environment. Adjustment may take place by adapting the self to the environment or by changing the environment. (From Campbell, Psychiatric Dictionary, 1996).

label: social behavior
semantic_ground_truth: Any behavior caused by or affecting another individual or group usually of the same species.

label: social conformity
semantic_ground_truth: Behavioral or attitudinal compliance with recognized social patterns or standards.

label: social desirability
semantic_ground_truth: A personality trait rendering the individual acceptable in social or interpersonal relations. It is related to social acceptance, social approval, popularity, social status, leadership qualities, or any quality making him a socially desirable companion.

label: psychological distance
semantic_ground_truth: The degree of a person's detachment from emotional involvement with people or situations.(APA Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms accessed 12/29/2020)

label: social dominance
semantic_ground_truth: Social structure of a group as it relates to the relative social rank of dominance status of its members. (APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

label: social facilitation
semantic_ground_truth: Any enhancement of a motivated behavior in which individuals do the same thing with some degree of mutual stimulation and consequent coordination.

label: social identification
semantic_ground_truth: The process by which an aspect of self image is developed based on in-group preference or ethnocentrism and a perception of belonging to a social or cultural group. (From APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

label: social isolation
semantic_ground_truth: The separation of individuals or groups resulting in the lack of or minimizing of social contact and/or communication. This separation may be accomplished by physical separation, by social barriers and by psychological mechanisms. In the latter, there may be interaction but no real communication.

label: social responsibility
semantic_ground_truth: The obligations and accountability assumed in carrying out actions or ideas on behalf of others.

label: social sciences
semantic_ground_truth: Disciplines concerned with the interrelationships of individuals in a social environment including social organizations and institutions. Includes Sociology and Anthropology.

label: social values
semantic_ground_truth: Abstract standards or empirical variables in social life which are believed to be important and/or desirable.

label: social work, psychiatric
semantic_ground_truth: Use of all social work processes in the treatment of patients in a psychiatric or mental health setting.

label: socioenvironmental therapy
semantic_ground_truth: Therapy whose primary emphasis is on the physical and social structuring of the environment to promote interpersonal relationships which will be influential in reducing behavioral disturbances of patients.

label: sociology
semantic_ground_truth: A social science dealing with group relationships, patterns of collective behavior, and social organization.

semantic_ground_truth: A parasomnia characterized by a partial arousal that occurs during stage IV of non-REM sleep. Affected individuals exhibit semipurposeful behaviors such as ambulation and are difficult to fully awaken. Children are primarily affected, with a peak age range of 4-6 years.

label: sound localization
semantic_ground_truth: Ability to determine the specific location of a sound source.

label: spatial behavior
semantic_ground_truth: Reactions of an individual or groups of individuals with relation to the immediate surrounding area including the animate or inanimate objects within that area.

label: speech
semantic_ground_truth: Communication through a system of conventional vocal symbols.

label: speech intelligibility
semantic_ground_truth: Ability to make speech sounds that are recognizable.

label: speech perception
semantic_ground_truth: The process whereby an utterance is decoded into a representation in terms of linguistic units (sequences of phonetic segments which combine to form lexical and grammatical morphemes).

label: stanford-binet test
semantic_ground_truth: An individual intelligence test designed primarily for school children to predict school performance and the ability to adjust to everyday demands.

label: reflex, startle
semantic_ground_truth: A complex involuntary response to an unexpected strong stimulus. The reaction involves physical movement away from the stimulus, MUSCLE CONTRACTION and limb flexion, BLINKING, and changes in HEART RATE, BLOOD PRESSURE, and RESPIRATION.

label: stereotyped behavior
semantic_ground_truth: Relatively invariant mode of behavior elicited or determined by a particular situation; may be verbal, postural, or expressive.

label: stereotyping
semantic_ground_truth: An oversimplified perception or conception especially of persons, social groups, etc.

label: stress, psychological
semantic_ground_truth: Stress wherein emotional factors predominate.

label: student dropouts
semantic_ground_truth: Individuals who leave school, secondary or college, prior to completion of specified curriculum requirements.

label: sublimation, psychological
semantic_ground_truth: A defense mechanism through which unacceptable impulses and instinctive urges are diverted into personally and socially acceptable channels; e.g., aggression may be diverted through sports activities.

label: substance withdrawal syndrome
semantic_ground_truth: Physiological and psychological symptoms associated with withdrawal from the use of a drug after prolonged administration or habituation. The concept includes withdrawal from smoking or drinking, as well as withdrawal from an administered drug.

label: sucking behavior
semantic_ground_truth: Any suction exerted by the mouth; response of the mammalian infant to draw milk from the breast. Includes sucking on inanimate objects. Not to be used for thumb sucking, which is indexed under fingersucking.

label: suggestion
semantic_ground_truth: The uncritical acceptance of an idea or plan of action.

label: suicide
semantic_ground_truth: The act of killing oneself.

label: suicide, attempted
semantic_ground_truth: The unsuccessful attempt to kill oneself.

label: superego
semantic_ground_truth: The component of the personality associated with ethics, standards, and self-criticism - the conscience. It is derived mainly from identification with parents and parent substitutes.

label: gestational carriers
semantic_ground_truth: Females who allow themselves to be impregnated with the understanding that the offspring are to be given over to the parents who have commissioned the surrogate.

label: taste
semantic_ground_truth: The ability to detect chemicals through gustatory receptors in the mouth, including those on the TONGUE; the PALATE; the PHARYNX; and the EPIGLOTTIS.

label: taste threshold
semantic_ground_truth: The minimum concentration at which taste sensitivity to a particular substance or food can be perceived.

label: temperament
semantic_ground_truth: Predisposition to react to one's environment in a certain way; usually refers to mood changes.

label: temperance
semantic_ground_truth: Habitual moderation in the indulgence of a natural appetite, especially but not exclusively the consumption of alcohol.

label: thermosensing
semantic_ground_truth: The sensation of cold, heat, coolness, and warmth as detected by THERMORECEPTORS.

label: territoriality
semantic_ground_truth: Behavior in defense of an area against another individual or individuals primarily of the same species.

label: test anxiety scale
semantic_ground_truth: A self-reporting test consisting of items concerning fear and worry about taking tests and physiological activity, such as heart rate, sweating, etc., before, during, and after tests.

label: psychotherapeutic processes
semantic_ground_truth: Experiential, attitudinal, emotional, or behavioral phenomena occurring during the course of treatment. label: thirst
semantic_ground_truth: A drive stemming from a physiological need for WATER.

label: transactional analysis
semantic_ground_truth: A psychoanalytic therapy wherein each social transaction is analyzed to determine the involved ego state (whether parent-like, child-like, or adult-like) as a basis for understanding behavior.

label: transference, psychology
semantic_ground_truth: The unconscious transfer to others (including psychotherapists) of feelings and attitudes which were originally associated with important figures (parents, siblings, etc.) in one's early life.

label: transsexualism
semantic_ground_truth: Expression of a GENDER IDENTITY inconsistent with, or not culturally-associated with the gender assigned to an individual at birth, combined with the desire to permanently transition to the gender with which they identify.

label: truth disclosure
semantic_ground_truth: Truthful revelation of information, specifically when the information disclosed is likely to be psychologically painful (bad news) to the recipient (e.g., revelation to a patient or a patient's family of the patient's DIAGNOSIS or PROGNOSIS) or embarrassing to the teller (e.g., revelation of medical errors).

label: type a personality
semantic_ground_truth: Established behavior pattern characterized by excessive drive and ambition, impatience, competitiveness, sense of time urgency, and poorly contained aggression.

label: unconscious, psychology
semantic_ground_truth: Those forces and content of the mind which are not ordinarily available to conscious awareness or to immediate recall.

label: verbal behavior
semantic_ground_truth: Includes both producing and responding to words, either written or spoken.

label: vision, ocular
semantic_ground_truth: The process in which light signals are transformed by the PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS into electrical signals which can then be transmitted to the brain.

label: vision, entoptic
semantic_ground_truth: Visual sensation derived from sensory stimulation by objects or shadows inside the eye itself, such as floating vitreous fibers, tissues, or blood.

label: visual acuity

(from Rev General Psychology, 15(4), 289–303. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0025754 accessed 8/11/2020)

label: information avoidance
semantic_ground_truth: Choosing to not obtain knowledge even if having the information could be to one's benefit.

label: disinformation
semantic_ground_truth: False information deliberately and often covertly spread in order to influence public opinion or obscure the truth. (https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/disinformation)

label: mentalization-based therapy
semantic_ground_truth: Mentalization-based therapy (MBT) is a type of long-term psychotherapy that is based on the use of MENTALIZATION.

label: vascular depression
semantic_ground_truth: Late-life depression associated with clinical or MRI defined cerebrovascular pathology.

label: adolescent mothers
semantic_ground_truth: Mothers aged less than 19 years at the time of child's conception or birth.

label: cognitive restructuring
semantic_ground_truth: A technique drawn from COGNITIVE BEHAVIOR THERAPY that helps an individual to identify, challenge and alter stress-inducing thought patterns and beliefs.

label: listening effort
semantic_ground_truth: The deliberate allocation of mental resources to overcome obstacles in goal pursuit when carrying out a task, with listening effort applied more when tasks involved listening. (From Pichora-Fuller et al.2016)

label: psychological first aid
semantic_ground_truth: Early psychosocial intervention approach used during or after traumatic life events as disasters, accidents, terrorist attacks causing negative effects on individual and/or society. It focuses on determining basic physical and mental needs of individuals in major events.

label: vaccination hesitancy
semantic_ground_truth: Delay in acceptance of vaccination despite availability.

label: microaggression
semantic_ground_truth: Brief verbal, behavioral, or situational indignities that communicate hostile, derogatory, or negative slights or insults. It may may be intentional or implicit. Three subtypes have been identified: microassaults, which are purposefully discriminatory actions; microinsults, which are subtle snubs that devalue a person’s identity; and microinvalidations, which are unintentional exclusions or negations of an individual’s thoughts. (dictionary.apa.org/microaggression 12/30/2020)

label: technology addiction
semantic_ground_truth: The inability to overcome a desire to have contact with and use technology and electronic devices.

label: adolescent fathers
semantic_ground_truth: Fathers initially aged less than 19 years at the time of their child's birth.

label: core stability
semantic_ground_truth: A POSTURE in which an ideal body mass distribution is achieved for the ABDOMINAL CORE. Abdominal core stability and balance provides the body an ability to maintain equilibrium and control of the SPINE and PELVIC REGION during movement.

label: cognitive psychology
semantic_ground_truth: Branch of psychology that explores the operation of mental processes related to perceiving, attending, thinking, language, and memory, mainly through inferences from behavior. (APA Dictionary of Psychology. https://dictionary.apa.org/cognitive-psychology, accessed 3/22/2021).

label: prolonged grief disorder
semantic_ground_truth: Severe and disabling grief reactions that do not remit in the 12 months after the death of a significant other. The core of the diagnosis includes persistent yearning or missing the deceased, and preoccupation with the circumstance of the death. (Carmassi, Clinical Handbook of Bereavement and Grief Reactions, 2018)

label: mass gatherings
semantic_ground_truth: Organized or spontaneous events where the number of people attending is sufficient to strain the planning and response resources of the community hosting the event. (WHO, 2008). These events include the gathering of people as the result of natural disasters or conflict.

label: ostracism
semantic_ground_truth: An extreme form of rejection in which one is excluded and ignored in the presence of others.

label: perceived discrimination
semantic_ground_truth: Perception of being treated badly or unfairly on the basis of race, ethnicity, gender, age, religion, physical appearance, sexual orientation, or other characteristics. This includes perceived discrimination in health care settings.

label: intersectional framework
semantic_ground_truth: Interconnections of social categorizations such as race, class, and gender, creating overlapping and interdependent systems of discrimination or disadvantage.

label: systemic racism
semantic_ground_truth: Processes of racism that are embedded in laws (local, state, and federal), policies, and practices of society and its institutions that provide advantages to racial groups deemed as superior, while differentially oppressing, disadvantaging, or otherwise neglecting racial groups viewed as inferior. Differential access to the goods, services, and opportunities of society by race. Institutionalized racism is normative, sometimes legalized, and often manifests as inherited disadvantage. It is structural, having been codified in our institutions of custom, practice, and law, so there need not be an identifiable perpetrator. (ttps://www.cdc.gov/chronicdisease/programs‐impact/sdoh.htm)

label: social cohesion
semantic_ground_truth: Strength of relationships and the sense of belongingness and solidarity among members of a community (https://www.healthypeople.gov/2020/topics-objectives/topic/social-determinants-health/interventions-resources/social-cohesion).

label: kinesiophobia
semantic_ground_truth: Anxiety disorder of persistent and irrational fear of movement following an injury. It is related to perceived disability due to injury and CATASTROPHIZING in fear of (anticipated) PAIN and possibility of REINJURY.

label: family support
semantic_ground_truth: Support systems that provide assistance and encouragement between and among members of a FAMILY.

label: family structure
semantic_ground_truth: Structural nature of relationships among members of a household typically in reference to a MINOR residing in the same home. More broadly any organizational framework that determines family membership, and the functions and hierarchical position of family members (https://eric.ed.gov/?qt=Family+Structure&ti=Family+Structure).

label: extended family
semantic_ground_truth: A household with members of at least three generations.

label: psychological well-being
semantic_ground_truth: Condition of existence, or state of awareness, in which psychological needs are satisfied

label: suicide prevention
semantic_ground_truth: Specific strategies for averting suicides. These include mental HEALTH PROMOTION and monitoring PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING and other intervention programs targeting susceptible individuals.

label: collective efficacy
semantic_ground_truth: A group belief and perception in its ability to complete a task successfully. It includes shared belief it can control deviant behavior of a member.

label: group dynamics
semantic_ground_truth: Processes of change in any social group from formation to functioning. It includes various forces that drive relationship among members and interaction with other groups.

label: theory of planned behavior
semantic_ground_truth: The construct in which intentions to perform behaviors of different kinds can be predicted with high accuracy from attitudes toward the behavior, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control; and these intentions, together with perceptions of behavioral control, account for considerable variance in actual behavior. (from Ajzen, Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes, V.50, Issue 2, p.179-211.)

label: intermittent fasting
semantic_ground_truth: Alternating between fasting for an extended period of time during the day and eating during a restricted time for the day.

historical_trace.history_note: 2023; use FASTING 2019-2022; for TIME RESTRICTED FEEDING use FASTING 2019-2022

label: mixed dementias
semantic_ground_truth: Dementias caused by multiple etiologies, e.g., ALZHEIMER DISEASE, and VASCULAR DEMENTIA and/or LEWY BODY DISEASE.

label: sleep duration
semantic_ground_truth: Total number of hours of sleep in a day.

label: chronotype
semantic_ground_truth: The natural inclination or preference of time of day in which an individual or an organism has the most activity, particularly as it relates to sleeping pattern and circadian sleep-wake preferences.

label: psychological safety
semantic_ground_truth: An environment where people are able to act and engage without fear of punishment or humiliation from others.

label: mental health teletherapy
semantic_ground_truth: Providing mental health services via TELECOMMUNICATIONS.

label: disability discrimination
semantic_ground_truth: Discrimination against persons with physical, intellectual, or psychiatric disabilities.

label: dignity therapy
semantic_ground_truth: Evidence-based psychotherapeutic modality for patients who are classified as terminally ill. Such patients may have loss of autonomy, severe physical pain, and challenging existential and spiritual experience, which contribute to disintegration of patient's sense of self.

label: compulsive sexual behavior disorder
semantic_ground_truth: Persistent pattern of failure to control intense, repetitive sexual impulses or urges resulting in repetitive sexual behavior. Symptoms may include repetitive sexual activities becoming a central focus of the person’s life to the point of neglecting health and personal care or other interests, activities and responsibilities; numerous unsuccessful efforts to significantly reduce repetitive sexual behavior; and continued repetitive sexual behavior despite adverse consequences or deriving little or no satisfaction from it. (https://icd.who.int/browse11/l-m/en#/http://id.who.int/icd/entity/1630268048)

label: psychological growth
semantic_ground_truth: A process of actively learning and adapting to new ways to function following a challenging life crisis.

semantic_ground_truth: Various techniques for actively managing a stressful event or situation.

label: emotional exhaustion
semantic_ground_truth: A state of feeling emotionally overextended and drained.

label: media exposure
semantic_ground_truth: The extent to which individuals encounter messages and content via COMMUNICATION MEDIA.

label: role conflict
semantic_ground_truth: A state of tension or distress that occurs when fulfilling roles of one status making it difficult to fulfill the roles of another.

label: subjective stress
semantic_ground_truth: Perceptions of PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS based on the individual's own personal values, beliefs and past and current experiences and circumstances.

label: time pressure
semantic_ground_truth: Sense of time urgency to complete a task. This sense of time urgency creates psychological pressure affecting performance (https://www.nrc.gov/docs/ML2112/ML21127A272.pdf).

label: emotional eating
semantic_ground_truth: Eating behaviors caused by PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; ANXIETY; BOREDOM; or other negative emotions rather than physical HUNGER.

label: body satisfaction
semantic_ground_truth: The subjective perception and evaluation of one’s own body in terms of different aspects such as size, shape, musculature or muscle tone, weight, and fitness.

label: nociplastic pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pain originating from the disrupted function of pain-related sensory pathways in both the peripheral and central nervous system (CNS), leading to heightened sensitivity.

label: grief therapy
semantic_ground_truth: Treatment that helps a person work through a greater than normal reaction to a loss, such as the death of a loved one.  Therapy may be individual or group therapy.

label: chemsex
semantic_ground_truth: The use of drugs to enhance or sustain sexual activity primarily but not exclusively by men who have sex with men.

label: sense of agency
semantic_ground_truth: Perception or feeling of control over one's own actions thereby influencing the course of events and outcomes. SELF-EFFICACY on the other hand is beliefs or expectations in self-ability to achieve intended goals or to produce a given effect in specific tasks.

label: mindfulness-based stress reduction
semantic_ground_truth: A therapeutic intervention designed to improve PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING through reduced ANXIETY; PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS; DISTRESS and improved mood by increased mindfulness.

label: mindfulness-based cognitive therapy
semantic_ground_truth: A therapeutic intervention designed to treat people with DEPRESSION through use of elements of MINDFULNESS-BASED STRESS REDUCTION and other cognitive behavioral therapy.

label: climate anxiety
semantic_ground_truth: Persistent and difficult to control psychological distress over CLIMATE CHANGE.

label: treatment expectations
semantic_ground_truth: Outcome anticipated or expected due to various qualities of a healthcare treatment.

label: outcome expectations
semantic_ground_truth: Believed or anticipated consequences of a person’s behavior.

label: auditory acuity
semantic_ground_truth: The ability to hear and distinguish one SOUND from another. These are typically assessed using whisper tests, tuning fork tests, or BONE CONDUCTION tests.

label: afterimage
semantic_ground_truth: Continuation of visual impression after cessation of stimuli causing the original image.

label: appetite
semantic_ground_truth: Natural recurring desire for food. Alterations may be induced by APPETITE DEPRESSANTS or APPETITE STIMULANTS.

label: arousal
semantic_ground_truth: Cortical vigilance or readiness of tone, presumed to be in response to sensory stimulation via the reticular activating system.

label: auditory fatigue
semantic_ground_truth: Loss of sensitivity to sounds as a result of auditory stimulation, manifesting as a temporary shift in auditory threshold. The temporary threshold shift, TTS, is expressed in decibels.

Temporary Threshold Shift, Auditory radiation effects

label: auditory perception
semantic_ground_truth: The process whereby auditory stimuli are selected, organized, and interpreted by the organism.

label: auditory threshold
semantic_ground_truth: The audibility limit of discriminating sound intensity and pitch.

label: back pain
semantic_ground_truth: Acute or chronic pain located in the posterior regions of the THORAX; LUMBOSACRAL REGION; or the adjacent regions.

label: bisexuality
semantic_ground_truth: The sexual attraction or relationship between members of both the same and the opposite SEX.

label: bone conduction
semantic_ground_truth: Transmission of sound waves through vibration of bones in the SKULL to the inner ear (COCHLEA). By using bone conduction stimulation and by bypassing any OUTER EAR or MIDDLE EAR abnormalities, hearing thresholds of the cochlea can be determined. Bone conduction hearing differs from normal hearing which is based on air conduction stimulation via the EAR CANAL and the TYMPANIC MEMBRANE.

label: bottle feeding
semantic_ground_truth: Use of nursing bottles for feeding. Applies to humans and animals.

label: breast feeding
semantic_ground_truth: The nursing of an infant at the breast.

label: chemotaxis
semantic_ground_truth: The movement of cells or organisms toward or away from a substance in response to its concentration gradient.

label: chest pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pressure, burning, or numbness in the chest.

label: child development
semantic_ground_truth: The continuous sequential physiological and psychological maturing of an individual from birth up to but not including ADOLESCENCE.

label: coitus
semantic_ground_truth: The sexual union of a male and a female, a term used for human only.

label: contraception behavior
semantic_ground_truth: Behavior patterns of those practicing CONTRACEPTION.

label: dominance, cerebral
semantic_ground_truth: Dominance of one cerebral hemisphere over the other in cerebral functions.

label: earache
semantic_ground_truth: Pain in the ear.

label: postural balance
semantic_ground_truth: A POSTURE in which an ideal body mass distribution is achieved. Postural balance provides the body carriage stability and conditions for normal functions in stationary position or in movement, such as sitting, standing, or walking.

label: escape reaction
semantic_ground_truth: Innate response elicited by sensory stimuli associated with a threatening situation, or actual confrontation with an enemy.

historical_trace.history_note: 68; FLIGHT REACTION was see under ESCAPE REACTION 1968-78

label: facial pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pain in the facial region including orofacial pain and craniofacial pain. Associated conditions include local inflammatory and neoplastic disorders and neuralgic syndromes involving the trigeminal, facial, and glossopharyngeal nerves. Conditions which feature recurrent or persistent facial pain as the primary manifestation of disease are referred to as FACIAL PAIN SYNDROMES.

label: fasting
semantic_ground_truth: Abstaining from FOOD.

label: feeding behavior
semantic_ground_truth: Behavioral responses or sequences associated with eating including modes of feeding, rhythmic patterns of eating, and time intervals.

label: figural aftereffect
semantic_ground_truth: A perceptual phenomenon used by Gestalt psychologists to demonstrate that events in one part of the perceptual field may affect perception in another part.

label: flicker fusion
semantic_ground_truth: The point or frequency at which all flicker of an intermittent light stimulus disappears.

label: food preferences
semantic_ground_truth: The selection of one food over another.

label: gagging
semantic_ground_truth: Contraction of the muscle of the PHARYNX caused by stimulation of sensory receptors on the SOFT PALATE, by psychic stimuli, or systemically by drugs.

label: galvanic skin response
semantic_ground_truth: A change in electrical resistance of the skin, occurring in emotion and in certain other conditions.

label: glossalgia
semantic_ground_truth: Painful sensations in the tongue, including a sensation of burning.

label: habituation, psychophysiologic
semantic_ground_truth: The disappearance of responsiveness to a repeated stimulation. It does not include drug habituation.

label: headache
semantic_ground_truth: The symptom of PAIN in the cranial region. It may be an isolated benign occurrence or manifestation of a wide variety of HEADACHE DISORDERS.

label: hearing
semantic_ground_truth: The ability or act of sensing and transducing ACOUSTIC STIMULATION to the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. It is also called audition.

label: higher nervous activity
semantic_ground_truth: A term used in Eastern European research literature on brain and behavior physiology for cortical functions. It refers to the highest level of integrative function of the brain, centered in the CEREBRAL CORTEX, regulating language, thought, and behavior via sensory, motor, and cognitive processes.

label: homosexuality
semantic_ground_truth: The sexual attraction or relationship between members of the same SEX.

label: human development
semantic_ground_truth: Continuous sequential changes which occur in the physiological and psychological functions during the life-time of an individual.

label: hunger
semantic_ground_truth: The desire for FOOD generated by a sensation arising from the lack of food in the STOMACH.

label: kinesthesis
semantic_ground_truth: Sense of movement of a part of the body, such as movement of fingers, elbows, knees, limbs, or weights.

label: functional laterality
semantic_ground_truth: Behavioral manifestations of cerebral dominance in which there is preferential use and superior functioning of either the left or the right side, as in the preferred use of the right hand or right foot.

label: loudness perception
semantic_ground_truth: The perceived attribute of a sound which corresponds to the physical attribute of intensity.

label: motor activity
semantic_ground_truth: Body movements of a human or an animal as a behavioral phenomenon.

label: neuralgia
semantic_ground_truth: Intense or aching pain that occurs along the course or distribution of a peripheral or cranial nerve.

label: orgasm
semantic_ground_truth: The climax of sexual excitement in either humans or animals.

label: pain
semantic_ground_truth: An unpleasant sensation induced by noxious stimuli which are detected by NERVE ENDINGS of NOCICEPTIVE NEURONS.

label: intractable pain
semantic_ground_truth: Persistent pain that is refractory to some or all forms of treatment.

label: postoperative pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pain during the period after surgery.

label: perceptual masking
semantic_ground_truth: The interference of one perceptual stimulus with another causing a decrease or lessening in perceptual effectiveness.

label: phosphenes
semantic_ground_truth: A subjective visual sensation with the eyes closed and in the absence of light. Phosphenes can be spontaneous, or induced by chemical, electrical, or mechanical (pressure) stimuli which cause the visual field to light up without optical inputs.

label: piloerection
semantic_ground_truth: Involuntary erection or bristling of hairs.

label: pitch discrimination
semantic_ground_truth: The ability to differentiate sound frequency or pitch.

label: pitch perception
semantic_ground_truth: A dimension of auditory sensation varying with cycles per second of the sound stimulus.

label: proprioception
semantic_ground_truth: Sensory functions that transduce stimuli received by proprioceptive receptors in joints, tendons, muscles, and the INNER EAR into neural impulses to be transmitted to the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. Proprioception provides sense of stationary positions and movements of one's body parts, and is important in maintaining KINESTHESIA and POSTURAL BALANCE.

label: psychomotor performance
semantic_ground_truth: The coordination of a sensory or ideational (cognitive) process and a motor activity.

label: reaction time
semantic_ground_truth: The time from the onset of a stimulus until a response is observed.

historical_trace.history_note: RESPONSE LATENCY was see under REACTION TIME 1970-76

label: reflex
semantic_ground_truth: An involuntary movement or exercise of function in a part, excited in response to a stimulus applied to the periphery and transmitted to the brain or spinal cord.

historical_trace.history_note: REFLEX, BABINSKI was BABINSKI REFLEX see under REFLEX, ABNORMAL 1968-89

label: sensation
semantic_ground_truth: The process in which specialized SENSORY RECEPTOR CELLS transduce peripheral stimuli (physical or chemical) into NERVE IMPULSES which are then transmitted to the various sensory centers in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

label: sleep
semantic_ground_truth: A readily reversible suspension of sensorimotor interaction with the environment, usually associated with recumbency and immobility.

label: sleep stages
semantic_ground_truth: Periods of sleep manifested by changes in EEG activity and certain behavioral correlates; they formerly included Stage 1: sleep onset, drowsy sleep; Stage 2: light sleep; Stages 3 and 4: delta sleep, light sleep, deep sleep, telencephalic sleep. In 2007, sleep stages were redefined by The American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) as: N1-N2 (sleep onset - light sleep), N3 (SLOW-WAVE SLEEP), and REM SLEEP.

label: sleep, rem
semantic_ground_truth: A stage of sleep characterized by rapid movements of the eye and low voltage fast pattern EEG. It is usually associated with dreaming.

label: smell
semantic_ground_truth: The ability to detect scents or odors, such as the function of OLFACTORY RECEPTOR NEURONS.

label: sound localization
semantic_ground_truth: Ability to determine the specific location of a sound source.

label: speech
semantic_ground_truth: Communication through a system of conventional vocal symbols.

label: speech intelligibility
semantic_ground_truth: Ability to make speech sounds that are recognizable.

label: speech perception
semantic_ground_truth: The process whereby an utterance is decoded into a representation in terms of linguistic units (sequences of phonetic segments which combine to form lexical and grammatical morphemes).

label: reflex, startle
semantic_ground_truth: A complex involuntary response to an unexpected strong stimulus. The reaction involves physical movement away from the stimulus, MUSCLE CONTRACTION and limb flexion, BLINKING, and changes in HEART RATE, BLOOD PRESSURE, and RESPIRATION.

label: taste
semantic_ground_truth: The ability to detect chemicals through gustatory receptors in the mouth, including those on the TONGUE; the PALATE; the PHARYNX; and the EPIGLOTTIS.

label: taste threshold
semantic_ground_truth: The minimum concentration at which taste sensitivity to a particular substance or food can be perceived.

label: thermosensing
semantic_ground_truth: The sensation of cold, heat, coolness, and warmth as detected by THERMORECEPTORS.

label: touch
semantic_ground_truth: Sensation of making physical contact with objects, animate or inanimate. Tactile stimuli are detected by MECHANORECEPTORS in the skin and mucous membranes.

label: vision, ocular
semantic_ground_truth: The process in which light signals are transformed by the PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS into electrical signals which can then be transmitted to the brain.

label: vision, entoptic
semantic_ground_truth: Visual sensation derived from sensory stimulation by objects or shadows inside the eye itself, such as floating vitreous fibers, tissues, or blood.

label: visual acuity
semantic_ground_truth: Clarity or sharpness of OCULAR VISION or the ability of the eye to see fine details. Visual acuity depends on the functions of RETINA, neuronal transmission, and the interpretative ability of the brain. Normal visual acuity is expressed as 20/20 indicating that one can see at 20 feet what should normally be seen at that distance. Visual acuity can also be influenced by brightness, color, and contrast.

label: visual fields
semantic_ground_truth: The total area or space visible in a person's peripheral vision with the eye looking straightforward.

label: wakefulness
semantic_ground_truth: A state in which there is an enhanced potential for sensitivity and an efficient responsiveness to external stimuli.

label: contrast sensitivity
semantic_ground_truth: The ability to detect sharp boundaries (stimuli) and to detect slight changes in luminance at regions without distinct contours. Psychophysical measurements of this visual function are used to evaluate VISUAL ACUITY and to detect eye disease.

label: vision disparity
semantic_ground_truth: The difference between two images on the retina when looking at a visual stimulus. This occurs since the two retinas do not have the same view of the stimulus because of the location of our eyes. Thus the left eye does not get exactly the same view as the right eye.

label: abdominal pain
semantic_ground_truth: Sensation of discomfort, distress, or agony in the abdominal region.

label: pain threshold
semantic_ground_truth: Amount of stimulation required before the sensation of pain is experienced.

label: pelvic pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pain in the pelvic region of genital and non-genital origin.

label: homosexuality, female
semantic_ground_truth: Sexual attraction or relationship between females.

label: neck pain
semantic_ground_truth: Discomfort or more intense forms of pain that are localized to the cervical region. This term generally refers to pain in the posterior or lateral regions of the neck.

label: heterosexuality
semantic_ground_truth: The sexual attraction or relationship between members of the opposite SEX.

label: shoulder pain
semantic_ground_truth: Unilateral or bilateral pain of the shoulder. It is often caused by physical activities such as work or sports participation, but may also be pathologic in origin.

label: flank pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pain emanating from below the RIBS and above the ILIUM.

label: uncertainty
semantic_ground_truth: The condition in which reasonable knowledge regarding risks, benefits, or the future is not available.

label: metatarsalgia
semantic_ground_truth: Pain in the region of the METATARSUS. It can include pain in the METATARSAL BONES; METATARSOPHALANGEAL JOINT; and/or intermetatarsal joints (TARSAL JOINTS).

label: adolescent development
semantic_ground_truth: The continuous sequential physiological and psychological changes during ADOLESCENCE, approximately between the age of 13 and 18.

label: reproductive behavior
semantic_ground_truth: Human behavior or decision related to REPRODUCTION.

label: freezing reaction, cataleptic
semantic_ground_truth: An induced response to threatening stimuli characterized by the cessation of body movements, except for those that are involved with BREATHING, and the maintenance of an immobile POSTURE.

label: immobility response, tonic
semantic_ground_truth: An induced response to threatening stimuli characterized by complete loss of muscle strength.

label: labor pain
semantic_ground_truth: Pain associated with OBSTETRIC LABOR in CHILDBIRTH. It is caused primarily by UTERINE CONTRACTION as well as pressure on the CERVIX; BLADDER; and the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT. Labor pain mostly occurs in the ABDOMEN; the GROIN; and the BACK.

label: referred pain
semantic_ground_truth: A type of pain that is perceived in an area away from the site where the pain arises, such as facial pain caused by lesion of the VAGUS NERVE, or throat problem generating referred pain in the ear.

historical_trace.history_note: 2007; for REFERRED FACIAL PAIN use FACIAL PAIN 2000-2006

label: color vision
semantic_ground_truth: Function of the human eye that is used in bright illumination or in daylight (at photopic intensities).
